nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: A simple one-step hydrothermal method was carried out to synthesize NiFe LDH using a Ti foil as substrate (denoted as NiFe LDH/Ti).
nodes.source_text: A simple one-step hydrothermal method was carried out to synthesize NiFe LDH using a Ti foil as substrate (denoted as NiFe LDH/Ti).

nodes.name: Ar⁺ ion irradiation of NiFe LDH
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti were irradiated by Ar⁺ ions with a certain energy of 100 keV to different fluences of 1×10¹⁵, 1×10¹⁶, 2×10¹⁶, 3×10¹⁶, and 4×10¹⁶ ions cm⁻² (denoted as ir-1e15, ir-1e16, ir-2e16, ir-3e16, ir-4e16, respectively). The optimized sample ir-2e16 forms NiO/NiFe₂O₄ heterostructure with rich oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH matches JPCDS No. 40-0215; after irradiation, NiFe LDH peaks decrease and new NiO {200} peak at 2θ=43.2° appears at 1×10¹⁶ ions cm⁻²; Ni peaks observed above 2×10¹⁶ ions cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of the as-prepared sample matches well with NiFe LDH (JPCDS No. 40-0215)... After Ar⁺ ions irradiation, the diffraction peaks of NiFe LDH decreased significantly... a new peak at 2θ = 43.2° which assign to the {200} planes of cubic NiO begin to appear.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH/Ti shows uniform nanosheet arrays with 1 μm thickness; ir-2e16 retains nanosheet structure with increased thickness and embedded nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti shows a uniformly grown nanosheet arrays structure with a film thickness of about 1 um... the nanosheet structure of the sample ir-2e16 is largely retained, while the thickness of nanosheets increases.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH shows 0.26 nm {012} spacing; ir-2e16 nanoparticles show 0.21 nm {200} NiO, 0.24 nm {111} NiO, 0.20 nm {111} Ni; crystalline/amorphous heterostructure observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of the as-prepared catalyst shows the interplanar spacing of 0.26 nm corresponding to the {012} lattice spacing of NiFe LDH... From the HRTEM images of these nanoparticles, the lattice fringes of 0.21 and 0.24 nm belonging to the {200} and {111} crystal planes of cubic NiO can be distinguished.

nodes.characterization_summary: ir-2e16 shows NiO crystals intermixed with amorphous domains indicating crystalline/amorphous heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: More notably, the HRTEM image of ir-2e16 shows that the sample are NiO crystals intermixed with amorphous domains. This indicates that crystalline/amorphous heterostructure is formed in the sample ir-2e16.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH shows Ni-O at 453, 539 cm⁻¹ and Fe-O at 695 cm⁻¹; irradiated samples show NiFe₂O₄ bands at 200, 323, 476, 561, 681 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, the peaks at 453 and 539 cm⁻¹ for the as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti can be assigned to the Ni-O stretching vibration and the peak at 695 cm⁻¹ ascribes to the Fe-O vibration... all of the irradiated samples exhibit five Raman bands at 200, 323, 476, 561, and 681 cm⁻¹, which correspond to the NiFe₂O₄ phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: ir-2e16 shows sextet signal similar to pure NiFe₂O₄ confirming amorphous NiFe₂O₄ phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S8, Supporting Information, the Mössbauer spectrum of the sample ir-2e16 at low temperature exists a similar sextet signal compared to that of pure NiFe₂O₄, indicating the existence of NiFe₂O₄ phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: ir-2e16 (NiO/NiFe₂O₄) has specific surface area 104.9 m²/g (1.38× higher than NiFe LDH 75.9 m²/g); type IV isotherm with hysteresis indicates mesopores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The sample NiO/NiFe₂O₄ (ir-2e16) exhibits a specific surface area of 104.9 m²g⁻¹, which is 1.38× higher than that of the as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti (75.9 m²g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH: Ni²⁺ at 856.0/873.6 eV, Fe³⁺ at 712.7 eV; ir-2e16: Ni²⁺ shift -0.5 eV, metallic Ni at 852.7/870.2 eV, new Fe³⁺ at 710.3 eV, O vacancy peak 531.9 eV increases, lattice oxide at 529.6 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti, high-resolution XPS for Ni 2p exists a pair of peaks at 856.0 and 873.6 eV corresponding to Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂... After Ar ions irradiation, the Ni²⁺ peaks of all the irradiated samples show a 0.5 eV negative shift... by calculating the proportion of the peak 531.9 eV in O 1s spectrum... the percentage of O vacancy for each irradiated sample increases dramatically.

nodes.characterization_summary: ir-2e16 shows stronger g=2.00 signal than NiFe LDH/Ti confirming rich oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S10, Supporting Information, the signals at g = 2.00 suggest that the structural defects come from oxygen vacancies, and the sample NiO/NiFe₂O₄ (ir-2e16) shows a stronger signal compared with NiFe LDH/Ti.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH shows O-H, H₂O, CO₃²⁻, M-OH peaks; irradiated samples show only metal-O-metal peaks below 600 cm⁻¹ indicating M-OH bond breakage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for the as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti, the absorption peaks at 3372, 1608, and 1345 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to... However, it can be found that only peaks below 600 cm⁻¹ appear for the irradiated samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: ir-2e16 C_dl = 0.9 mF cm⁻² (15× NiFe LDH 0.062 mF cm⁻², 4.5× NiFe₂O₄ 0.21 mF cm⁻², 10× NiO 0.093 mF cm⁻²) indicating highest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S17, Supporting Information and Figure 4e, the C_dl of the NiO/NiFe₂O₄ (ir-2e16) (0.9 mF cm⁻¹) is 15×, 4.5× and 10× of the as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti (0.062 mF cm⁻¹) pure NiFe₂O₄ (0.21 mF cm⁻¹),and NiO (0.093 mF cm⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: ir-2e16 shows much smaller R_ct than NiFe LDH and ir-1e15 indicating higher conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be found that the high-fluence irradiated samples show much smaller charge transfer resistance than that of the as-prepared NiFe LDHs/Ti and the sample ir-1e15.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH has Ni:Fe atom ratio of 2.39:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: with atom ratio of 2.39:1 for Ni and Fe basing on EDS measurement, Table S2, Supporting Information.
